facts.statement: Caulkicephalus is a genus of anhanguerid pterosaur found on the Isle of Wight off the coast of England.
facts.quote: Caulkicephalus is a genus of anhanguerid pterosaur from the Isle of Wight off the coast of England.

facts.statement: Caulkicephalus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived during the Early Cretaceous period, about 125 million years ago.

facts.statement: Bone fragments of an unknown pterosaur were discovered between 1995 and 2003 at the Yaverland locality near Sandown.
facts.quote: Between 1995 and 2003, bone fragments of an unknown pterosaur were found at the Yaverland locality near Sandown.

facts.statement: The genus Caulkicephalus was named and described in 2005 by Lorna Steel, David Martill, David Unwin, and John Winch.
facts.quote: In 2005 a new genus was named and described by Lorna Steel, David Martill, David Unwin and John Winch.

facts.statement: The combined length of the preserved snout fragments is 290 mm.
facts.quote: The snout fragments have a combined length of 290 mm.

facts.statement: A constriction in the snout with larger teeth at the broad end, known as a "prey grab," is interpreted as an adaptation for catching slippery prey like fish.
facts.quote: The smaller sized teeth were placed in a constriction of the snout, which thus had a broader end with larger teeth, a so-called "prey grab", usually interpreted as an adaptation to catch slippery prey such as fish.

facts.statement: The presence of land plant debris in the fossil layer suggests Caulkicephalus may have inhabited a more terrestrial environment.
facts.quote: The layer the fossils were found in, does not consist of marine sediments, but contains land plant debris; this is seen as an indication of a more terrestrial habitat.

facts.statement: Studies in 2019 reassigned Caulkicephalus to the family Anhangueridae, subfamily Anhanguerinae, as a sister taxon to Guidraco and Ludodactylus.
facts.quote: In 2019 however, several studies have reassigned Caulkicephalus to the family Anhangueridae, specifically to the subfamily Anhanguerinae, sister taxon to both Guidraco and Ludodactylus.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Caulkicephalus to the family Ornithocheiridae based on the narrowing in the middle of the snout, a classification later revised.
facts.quote: Caulkicephalus was by the describers assigned to the Ornithocheiridae in view of the narrowing in the middle of the snout.

facts.statement: Fossil fragments of an unknown pterosaur were discovered between 1995 and 2003 at Yaverland near Sandown.
facts.quote: Entre 1995 y 2003 fragmentos de huesos de un pterosaurio desconocido fueron hallados en la localidad de Yaverland cerca de Sandown.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in brown clay from the Wessex Formation of the Wealden Group, dating to the Early Cretaceous (Barremian), approximately 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los descubrimientos fueron efectuados en una capa de arcilla parda de la Formación Wessex del Grupo Wealden, que data del Cretácico Inferior (en el Barremiense, hace cerca de 130 millones de años).

facts.statement: The new genus was described in 2005 by Lorna Steel, David Martill, David Unwin, and John Winch.
facts.quote: En 2005 un nuevo género y descrito por Lorna Steel, David Martill, David Unwin y John Winch.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Caulkhead", a traditional nickname for Wight island residents, with the Greek word kephale meaning "head".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de "Caulkhead", un apodo tradicional para los residentes de la isla de Wight, y del término griego kephale, "cabeza".

facts.statement: The species name trimicrodon means "three small teeth", referring to its dentition.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, trimicrodon, significa "tres pequeños dientes", en referencia a su dentición.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of three roughly contiguous pieces from the front of the snout.
facts.quote: El holotipo es IWCMS 2002.189.1, 2, 4: tres piezas, más o menos contiguas, del frente del hocico.

facts.statement: The combined length of the snout fragments is 290 millimeters.
facts.quote: Los fragmentos del hocico tiene una longitud combinada de 290 milímetros.

facts.statement: A crest is present on top of the snout, which does not have a rounded tip.
facts.quote: Sobre la parte superior del hocico se encuentra una cresta, que no llegaba a ser de punta redondeada.

facts.statement: The teeth increased in size until the third pair, which were the longest.
facts.quote: Los dientes incrementaban de tamaño hasta el tercer par de dientes que eran los más largos.

facts.statement: The fourth tooth pair matched the first in size, while the fifth, sixth, and seventh pairs were notably smaller, less than half the size, a feature referenced in the species name.
facts.quote: El cuarto par era igual al primero mientras que el quinto, sexto y séptimo eran notablemente menores, menos de la mitad de tamaño; es a esta característica a la que hace referencia su nombre de especie.

facts.statement: Small teeth were located in a compressed area of the snout ending in a wide tip with large teeth, forming a "trap" generally believed to be an adaptation for catching elusive prey like fish.
facts.quote: Los dientes menores estaban situados en una área comprimida del hocico, la cual tenía un amplio extremo final con grandes dientes, formando así una especie de "trampa", que se cree generalmente que era una adaptación para capturar presas escurridizas como los peces.

facts.statement: A damaged posterior cranial fragment shows the base of a parietal crest on top, which likely pointed backward.
facts.quote: El fragmento craneal posterior, un neurocráneo dañado, muestra en su parte superior la base de una cresta parietal, que probablemente apuntaba hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The describers assigned Caulkicephalus to the family Ornithocheiridae due to the narrowing in the middle of the snout.
facts.quote: Caulkicephalus fue asignado por sus descriptores a la familia Ornithocheiridae en vista de su estrechamiento en la mitad del hocico.

facts.statement: The snout crest indicated membership in the broader group Ornithocheiroidea, while the parietal crest was suggested as a shared trait of the narrower group Euornithocheira.
facts.quote: La cresta del hocico fue vista como una indicación de que pertenecía al grupo más general Ornithocheiroidea sensu Unwin, mientras que la cresta parietal fue sugerida como una sinapomorfia, un rasgo nuevo compartido, del más estrecho grupo Euornithocheira.

facts.statement: David Martill estimated that Caulkicephalus had a wingspan of nearly five meters.
facts.quote: David Martill estimó que Caulkicephalus tenía una envergadura de cerca de cinco metros.

facts.statement: The time range for Caulkicephalus is the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Caulkicephalus is Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithocheiridae

facts.statement: Caulkicephalus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Caulkicephalus is Caulkicephalus trimicrodon.
facts.quote: Type species: Caulkicephalus trimicrodon

facts.statement: The fossil layer contained terrestrial plant residues rather than marine sediments, suggesting a possible terrestrial habitat.
facts.quote: La capa en la cual se hallaron sus fósiles no consistía de sedimentos marinos, sino que contenía residuos de plantas terrestres; esto es una posible indicación de un hábitat terrestre.
